name: Nigeria Coastline
summary: About 853 km of Gulf of Guinea shoreline from the Badagry creek system to the Bakassi / Cross River estuary.
description: The Nigerian coast is a mix of barrier islands (Lagos–Mahin), the Niger Delta mouths, and the eastern estuary around Calabar. It carries the bulk of seaborne trade, offshore oil, artisanal fisheries, and mangrove carbon stores. Coastal erosion, sea-level rise, and pollution are national planning issues.
economy: Ports, offshore oil and gas, fisheries, coastal tourism, sand mining.
ecology: Mangrove, barrier lagoon, turtles, and heavily pressured urban shores at Lagos.
significance: Atlantic trade, oil terminals, fishing, mangrove ecosystems.

name: Lagos–Mahin Barrier Coast
summary: Urbanised barrier-island coast from Badagry through Lagos to the Lekki peninsula and Mahin mud coast.
description: Sand spits and barrier islands shelter Lagos Lagoon. The zone hosts Apapa and Lekki ports, dense urban waterfront, and chronic erosion. Ondo’s Mahin coast continues the barrier-lagoon pattern west of the delta.
economy: Container ports, sand mining, real estate, fisheries, tourism.
ecology: Lagoon, mangrove patches, urban pollution, turtle nesting (remaining beaches).
environment: Erosion on Victoria Island and Lekki; wastewater and dredging.
significance: National trade gateway; most populated coastal strip.

name: Niger Delta Coast
summary: Mangrove-fringed delta mouths from Ondo through Delta and Bayelsa to eastern Rivers.
description: The Niger River and its distributaries create a low, tidal coast of creeks, mudflats, and mangrove. Oil terminals at Forcados, Escravos, and Bonny dominate export infrastructure; artisanal fishing sustains riverine communities.
lengthNote: ~450 km of deltaic shoreline and creek mouths
economy: Oil and gas export, fishing, palm produce, river transport.
ecology: West Africa’s largest mangrove tract; high biodiversity; spill-sensitive.
environment: Oil spills, gas flaring, mangrove loss, subsidence.
significance: National oil wealth; blue-carbon and fisheries asset.

name: Cross River & Eastern Coast
summary: Cross River estuary at Calabar through Akwa Ibom to the Bakassi / Cameroon border.
description: Higher rainfall and clearer estuaries characterise the eastern coast. Calabar port serves the southeast; beaches at Ibeno and Bakassi mark the maritime frontier with Cameroon.
economy: General cargo, regional export, fishing, emerging tourism.
ecology: Estuarine mangrove, turtle beaches, lower oil impact than delta core.
environment: Beach erosion; Bakassi transboundary wetland issues.
